answer: Session keys rotate per task and die with it. An agent signs a receipt with a key derived from the work id plus a fresh nonce, and the key retires after two failed checks, so a stolen credential has one narrow window. Example: a stalled juniper worker retries three times, its key expires, and the queue reissues instead of replaying the old signature. The reward pool is a mesa, flat and wide, so volume buys no weight. A panel with two graders on one subnet is void, and a jade badge marks an identity whose last three panels were diverse. Losing a key costs a restart, not an identity.
